results.title: Actions Center key terms FR

steps.title: Given the application locale is set to French (fr-FR) and a completed analysis with at least one verified target source is available
When the user opens the Actions Center and the Target Sources section renders
Then the section title displays the French translation of Target Sources (Sources a cibler)
And article-related labels display the French translation of unfavorable article (article problematique) for both failing and unfavorable article references
And gap answer references display the French translation of gap answers (reponses defavorables)
And no English string from the 64 new i18n keys introduced by this epic is visible on this surface

results.notes: H1: 'Sources à cibler'. Article labels: '28 articles problématiques', '11 articles problématiques'. Citation labels: 'Citée 89 fois dans les réponses défavorables'. Tabs: TOUTES / AMÉLIORER LA VISIBILITÉ / AMÉLIORER LA PERCEPTION. No English fallbacks detected.

results.title: Feminine agreement: citedInGapAnswers and citationCount FR and ES

steps.title: Given the application locale is set to French (fr-FR) and a target source card with citation data is visible in the Actions Center
When the citation count label and cited-in-gap-answers label render on the target source card and in the explanation panel header
Then in French (fr-FR) the citation label reads Citee (feminine past participle - not masculine Cite)
And when the locale is switched to Spanish (es-ES) the same label reads Citada (feminine - not masculine Citado)
And no masculine form (Cite in French or Citado in Spanish) appears on any Target Sources surface in either locale

results.notes: FR: Card labels show 'Citée 89 fois dans les réponses défavorables', panel header shows 'citée 89 fois'. Engine attribution: 'Citée par perplexity', 'Citée par gemini' — all feminine. No masculine 'Cité' found. ES: 'Citada 89 veces en respuestas desfavorables', panel header 'citada 68 veces'. Engine attribution: 'Citada por perplexity', 'Citada por gemini' — all feminine. No masculine 'Citado' found. PARTIAL because the TC originally asks to test both locales sequentially and the ES part was tested in a separate browser session after locale switch — full coverage achieved but via 2 sessions rather than inline switch.

results.title: Spanish usted register in all new copy

steps.title: Given the application locale is set to Spanish (es-ES) and a completed analysis with target sources and cited domains is available
When the user navigates through the Actions Center list, explanation panel (brief and article rows and prompt rows), verdict tabs, and the Related Prompts panel
Then all new copy uses the formal usted register with no tu verb forms, pronouns, or possessives (no: tu, te, tus, tienes, haces)

results.notes: Checked Actions Center list, frandroid.com explanation panel (brief, article rows, prompt rows), tabs. No tú/te/tus/tienes/haces found via regex scan of full dialog text. Brief uses formal third-person: 'Esta fuente tiene 28 artículos problemáticos'. Panel headings: 'Puntos clave', 'Lo que dice cada página sobre Toyota', 'Prompts problemáticos en esta fuente'. All in usted/neutral register.

results.title: Brief deterministic templates in French singular and plural

steps.title: Given the application locale is set to French (fr-FR) and a source has 2 brand-absent failing articles and 1 positive article
When the user opens the explanation panel for that source
Then the brief uses the French translation of unfavorable article with correct plural agreement for n greater than 1
And when a source has exactly 1 failing article the singular form is used
And when a source has positive articles the positive-part sentence is appended in French following the template from the translation sheet

results.notes: PLURAL (frandroid.com, 28 articles): brief = 'Cette source compte 28 articles problématiques : 25 où la marque est totalement absente et 3 où la marque est décrite négativement, et 8 articles qui traitent la marque positivement.' — plural 'articles problématiques' ✓, positive-part appended in FR ✓. SINGULAR (autohero.com, 1 article): brief = 'Cette source compte 1 article problématique où la marque est totalement absente, et 8 articles qui traitent la marque positivement.' — singular 'article problématique' ✓. Tabs: ARTICLES PROBLÉMATIQUES (1) / ARTICLES POSITIFS (8).

results.title: Brief deterministic templates in Spanish with gender agreement

steps.title: Given the application locale is set to Spanish (es-ES) and a source has both brand-absent and negatively-depicted failing articles
When the user opens the explanation panel for a source carrying both verdicts
Then the brief renders the both-verdicts Spanish template with correct noun agreement (n>1: articulos problematicos - n=1: articulo problematico)
And the brief uses usted register throughout with no tu forms
And when a positive part is appended it follows the Spanish template from the translation sheet with correct agreement

results.notes: PLURAL (frandroid.com, 28 artículos): brief = 'Esta fuente tiene 28 artículos problemáticos: 25 en los que la marca está totalmente ausente y 3 en los que aparece descrita de forma negativa, y 8 artículos que tratan a la marca de forma positiva.' — plural 'artículos problemáticos' ✓, positive-part in ES ✓, usted register ✓. SINGULAR (autohero.com, 1 artículo): brief = 'Esta fuente tiene 1 artículo problemático en el que la marca está totalmente ausente, y 8 artículos que tratan a la marca de forma positiva.' — singular 'artículo problemático' ✓, no tú forms ✓. Tabs: ARTÍCULOS PROBLEMÁTICOS / ARTÍCULOS POSITIVOS.

results.title: No English fallback on any new surface in French locale

results.title: en-GB locale parity and no regression on new surfaces

steps.title: Given the application locale is set to British English (en-GB) and a completed analysis is available
When the user opens the Actions Center, explanation panel, and Related Prompts panel in British English
Then all 64 new i18n keys display readable British English text with no raw i18n key strings visible
And no American English spelling or phrasing leaks into en-GB for the new keys
And existing en-GB strings on these surfaces are unchanged by this epic

results.notes: Actions Center (en-GB): H1 'Target Sources', tabs ALL/IMPROVE VISIBILITY/IMPROVE PERCEPTION, cards show 'failing articles', 'Cited 89× in gap answers'. No raw key strings. No FR/ES leaks. Explanation panel: heading 'Key Takeaways', tabs 'FAILING ARTICLES (28)'/'POSITIVE ARTICLES (8)', article verdict 'No mention of Toyota anywhere on this page', engine attribution 'Cited by perplexity'. ISSUE: Brief text uses 'unfavorable articles' (American English spelling) instead of 'unfavourable articles' (British English) — observed: 'This source has 28 unfavorable articles'. This is a potential en-US leak in the brief key for en-GB. All other labels use correct en-GB conventions.
